title: QUIZ - 92
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Interpreting Positive and Negative Relationships in Graphs
questions.learningObjective: Interpret whether a graph shows a positive or negative relationship between two variables
questions.question: On a graph showing quantity sold versus demand, if the graph shows that as demand increases, quantity sold increases, what does this indicate about their relationship?

options.label: A
options.text: The variables are always exactly equal to each other.

options.label: B
options.text: A positive relationship: the two variables tend to increase or decrease together.

options.label: C
options.text: No relationship exists between the two variables.

options.label: D
options.text: A negative relationship: as one variable increases, the other tends to decrease.

questions.explanation: Since demand increases while quantity sold increases, the graph shows a positive relationship (both move in the same direction).
questions.hint: Check whether the two variables move in the same direction (positive relationship) or opposite directions (negative relationship).

questions.concept: Calculating Total Change from a Constant Rate
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the total change in output resulting from a given change in input at a constant rate
questions.question: A graph shows a constant rate of change of 7 meters per unit of input. If the input increases by 14 units, by how much does the output change?

options.label: A
options.text: 98 meters

options.label: B
options.text: 105 meters

options.label: C
options.text: 14 meters

options.label: D
options.text: 7 meters

questions.explanation: Total change in output = rate \(\times\) change in input \(= 7 \times 14 = 98\) meters.
questions.hint: Multiply the constant rate of change by the amount the input changed.
